correctness.rationale: A complete combinatorial proof gives the exact longest path length min(s,2(s-L)+1) for every selected multipartite occupancy. From its exact feasibility predicate, one-vertex extensions are analyzed in both directions, including the whole-graph \(P_k\)-free boundary, giving two disjoint maximal types. Unique dominant parts prevent double counting in both polynomials. For all tested 557 part-vector and path-order instances, an independent adjacency-path search over 320576 subsets matches every all-set and maximal-set coefficient. The parity and gap consequences follow by exact algebra; the finite experiment is not substituted for proof.

originality.rationale: The full accessible Bujtás–Jakovac–Tuza 2021 source discusses general bounds and chordal graphs, not complete multipartite maximal-set cardinality polynomials. The directly relevant Li–Zuo 2018 contribution establishes scalar complete-bipartite minimum numbers, independently quoted as Tu 2022 Theorems 37–38; the new count polynomials strictly refine these values and distinguish many nonoptimal inclusion-minimal transversals. The longest-path occupancy criterion and the \(k=3\) dissociation boundary are explicitly prior. Exact-claim and alias searches of the accessible published records and literature did not identify an equivalent complete classification. Priority remains provisional because the 2018 full text was unavailable.
residual_risks: The complete text of Li–Zuo 2018 was inaccessible; an unindexed exact enumeration could exist there or elsewhere.
An all-parameter classification may be independently derivable from the classical occupancy criterion, so publication priority and perceived novelty warrant an independent literature review.
The comparison uses accessible literature and indexed published records, not exhaustive mathematical publication coverage.

value.rationale: Minimal k-path transversals are a natural graph-covering object connected to network protection, and full labeled cardinality distributions for arbitrary complete multipartite graphs and every \(k\ge4\) refine known scalar optima. A sharp even/odd bipartite transition governs whether all inclusion-minimal covers have one or two sizes, while in odd order they exhibit arbitrarily long support gaps and a quantified rare small-cover fraction, revealing behavior invisible to minimum-cardinality results. The statement is a complete structural classification, not an arbitrary finite lookup or cosmetic renaming.
